newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Havel heads for Indian reserve in Brazilian Amazon.
newsitem.headline: Havel heads for Indian reserve in Brazilian Amazon.

text.p: Czech Republic President Vaclav Havel headed off on Tuesday to visit an Indian tribe in the Amazon rain forest, officials said.

Havel, who is on a week-long tour of Latin America's largest country, flew from the Brazilian capital, Brasilia, to the Amazonian capital, Manaus. There he was due to see the Amazonas Theatre, known as the Manaus Opera.
A domed neoclassical building built 100 years ago as a monument to the rubber wealth created by the jungle, the opera fell into decay until a million-dollar renovation in 1990.
On Wednesday the Czech president will fly deep into the Amazon basin for a two-hour visit with the Waimiri-Atroari Indian tribe. Later he will travel to Brazil's industrial heartland, Sao Paulo.

On Saturday, Havel will pay a visit to the city of Lidice in the interior of Rio de Janeiro state, named after the Czech town the Nazis destroyed in the Second World War in retaliation for a Czech partisan attack on a German general.
He was due to leave Brazil on Sept. 21 and head for Chile. After Chile he was scheduled to tour Argentina and Uruguay, two of Brazil's partners in the Mercosur customs union.
Havel will return briefly to Brazil for a spot of sightseeing at the spectacular Foz de Iguacu waterfalls before flying back to Prague on Sept. 28.
